clue.text: Heard solver initially gets kudos, cracking puzzle

indicators.note: cracking breaks the word kudos apart so its letters can be rebuilt with the extra one
the solver is addressed as 'you', and that word heard aloud is the letter U

parts.note: the solver of a crossword is 'you'

explanation.surface: The solver, having cracked a tough puzzle, earns praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' turns 'solver' (you) into the letter U; 'cracking' scrambles KUDOS plus that U.
explanation.definitionFit: This number-placing grid game is a well-known kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Sneaky way to get fit topless

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, which in a down answer is the first letter

parts.note: fit means in good health

explanation.surface: A cheeky shortcut to getting in shape: going without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes H from HEALTHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy movement is quiet and furtive, done so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Cross-dressing apparel's kept somewhat drier

indicators.note: the apparel has kept the other word, holding it within

parts.note: drag is clothing of the opposite sex, worn by a performer
-ish is a suffix meaning somewhat

explanation.surface: A cross-dresser's outfit stays rather on the dry side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drier' is not a comparative adjective here but a noun: a cloth that dries the dishes, held by 'kept'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth used to wipe and dry plates is a drier, though the word more often names a washcloth.

clue.text: Wiping up sauce boat

indicators.note: wiping removes something, here that small word from the end of the sauce

parts.note: ketchup is a tomato sauce

explanation.surface: Mopping up a spill from a gravy boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wiping' takes UP off KETCHUP. The surface 'sauce boat' is a gravy jug, but here 'boat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing vessel is a type of boat.

clue.text: Help to recall retreating soldiers during day in charge

indicators.note: during places one thing within the span of another, so the reversed soldiers sit inside the day

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

indicators.note: retreating soldiers go backwards, so the word for them is read in reverse

parts.note: men is a common word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A military picture: troops pulling back on a day when someone is in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' signals the reversal and 'during' the insertion; the day is abbreviated to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory aid, such as a rhyme for remembering facts, is a help to recall.

clue.text: Number 20 pulls out matches that won't set the world on fire

definitions.text: matches that won't set the world on fire

parts.note: a score is twenty
to draw is to pull out, as a weapon or a card

explanation.surface: A footballer wearing shirt 20 pulls out of a dull fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The matches are football games ending nil-nil, the dullest results.
explanation.definitionFit: Goalless tied football games are famously dull, so they won't set the world on fire, an idiom for excite.

clue.text: Philosopher has terribly inane periods

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a British philosopher

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of inane are jumbled

explanation.surface: A thinker takes a pretty silly line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns INANE into ENNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spans of a thousand years are very long periods of time.

clue.text: Undoing Natalie's jacket I covered in jam

indicators.note: a jacket is the outside layer, so take the outer letters of the name
the I is covered by the jam word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a mess, as in being in a jam, a predicament

explanation.surface: A woman's jacket gets smeared with jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' looks like the fruit spread, but here it is a predicament; 'covered in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's downfall or ruin, the thing that brings about their undoing.

clue.text: Jug in the fridge, perhaps

definitions.meaning: jug is slang for prison, as is this word
describing food that is chillier, as fridge contents are

explanation.surface: A milk jug sitting in the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug' looks like a container; it is slang for jail. 'in the fridge' is an example of being more chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: slang for a prison, and the comparative of cool, meaning chillier.

clue.text: Everton's lead star trashed unknown substitute

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, here of Everton's
trashed means wrecked, so the letters of star are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Z is one of the algebraic letters for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A football report: Everton's top player is slated and a little-known replacement comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashed' turns STAR into RSAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation stand-in for the real thing is a substitute, as with wartime fake coffee.

clue.text: Hint of olive oil, some tossed: an Italian standard

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its opening letter, here of olive
tossed as in a salad, so the letters of oil and some are mixed up

explanation.surface: A recipe: a touch of olive oil tossed through, with an Italian flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' rearranges OILSOME into SOLEMIO.
explanation.definitionFit: This Neapolitan song is a classic, much-covered standard of the Italian repertoire.

clue.text: One wearing fine tank-top out maybe mugged thus

indicators.note: the clothes in the surface wrap round the one, so it is placed within
out means disordered, so the letters of fine and tank-top are scattered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in a smart tank-top steps out and is robbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles FINETANKTOP and 'wearing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being threatened with a blade is how a person might be robbed in a street mugging.

clue.text: Run into US city slum at a leisurely pace

indicators.note: into signals that the run goes inside the city-and-slum pair, between them

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a ghetto is a run-down, deprived area of a city
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a deprived area of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the insertion; 'Run' looks like the verb but is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning fairly slowly, a little quicker than largo.

clue.text: Republican's left to guarantee result

indicators.note: left means departed, so that letter goes out of the guarantee word

parts.note: to guarantee something is to make sure of it
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican walks out to secure a political outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' tells you R has gone, leaving the word without it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to result means to follow as a consequence, which is the same sense.

clue.text: Majesty's clothing given imperious quality

indicators.note: clothing wraps around something, so the royal title goes round the word for given

parts.note: Highness is a royal title, like Majesty
handed means given

explanation.surface: A royal's wardrobe is said to give them a lofty air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like a noun about the wardrobe but is the insertion signal: one word wraps the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogant, overbearing behaviour is an imperious trait in a person.

clue.text: Ethanol is drunk, a drop of something hard

indicators.note: drunk means in a disorderly state, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Alcohol hits hard: a tot of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a drop of something hard' looks like a shot of strong liquor, but it is a falling pellet of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice falling from a storm cloud is a drop of frozen, solid water.

clue.text: Italian side like Liverpool in the ground

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club
Liverpool FC play in red and are known as the Reds

explanation.surface: An Italian football team taking the field like Liverpool at their stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the ground' looks like a stadium, but means buried.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has been buried lies beneath the earth.

clue.text: Note evil establishment's fake news

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
sin is evil or wrongdoing
formation is the establishment or founding of something

explanation.surface: A wicked organisation peddles false stories.
explanation.definitionFit: False information spread deliberately or by mistake is what people call fake news.

clue.text: Unsophisticated girl and Frank moving in

indicators.note: moving shifts the letters of the honest word into a new order

parts.note: genuine and frank both mean sincere and honest

explanation.surface: A naive young woman and a man named Frank set up home together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but means honest.
explanation.definitionFit: An innocent, naive young woman, especially as a stock theatre role.

clue.text: Take off tie, and I'm at work!

indicators.note: to work something is to manipulate it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An office worker loosening their tie on arrival at the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like removing the tie, but means mimic. 'work' rearranges TIEIMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to impersonate or mimic them.

clue.text: Like nosh the European President's almost thrown up

indicators.note: thrown up means going upward, so in this down answer the letters are reversed

parts.note: el is 'the' in Spanish, a European language

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the president's name goes

parts.note: Joe Biden, US President when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A politician vomiting after a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BIDEN to BIDE; 'thrown up' reverses ELBIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is British slang for food, so something like nosh is fit to eat.

clue.text: Perhaps suck the oxygen out of artist

definitions.meaning: to remove gas from something; oxygen is one example of a gas
Edgar ..., the French painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: Taking the air out of a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as de-gas it means remove gas; whole, it is the Impressionist painter's surname.

clue.text: Cable from detainee I don't know, short message

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war
er is the hesitant sound of someone unsure
to drop someone a line is to send a short note

explanation.surface: A cable arrives from a prisoner who sends only a vague, brief note.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhead wire carrying electricity is a cable strung between pylons.

clue.text: Sack or fire one

definitions.meaning: to sack is to plunder or ransack
a gun for shooting, a thing you fire

explanation.surface: Dismiss or fire a worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' and 'fire' both suggest dismissal, but one means ransack and the other a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to search and plunder, and also names a long-barrelled gun.

clue.text: Warmth from aristocrat backing US neighbour

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the aristocrat word is reversed

parts.note: a nob is a British slang word for a toff or aristocrat
homie is American slang for someone from your neighbourhood

explanation.surface: An upper-class person supports their American neighbour with warm feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses NOB to BON. NOB is British slang for a wealthy or upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured friendliness is a kind of social warmth.

clue.text: Not broadcasting old dalliance, a non- starter

indicators.note: a non-starter has lost its opening, so the first letter, a, is taken off the dalliance

parts.note: an affair is a casual romantic dalliance

explanation.surface: An old fling that never got going stays off the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a non-starter' removes the first letter A from AFFAIR, leaving FFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme or presenter not currently transmitting is not broadcasting.

clue.text: He and I, say, heating devices

definitions.meaning: He (helium) and I (iodine) are chemical symbols for two examples of these
the coils in a kettle or oven that get hot

explanation.surface: Two people compared to heaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium and iodine are chemical substances in the periodic table; heating coils in appliances share the name.

clue.text: Key aspect of female gender and male gender

indicators.note: an aspect is a part, so the letters are a piece of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A main point about how women and men are seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The same six letters sit inside both 'female gender' and 'male gender'.
explanation.definitionFit: The key on a map or chart, explaining its symbols, is also called by this name.
